summary: SSE mid-stream concatenated fragments and missing end-marker after upstream proxy abrupt RST
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated occurrences where server-sent event (SSE) streams terminate with the final JSON payload missing and preceding fragments concatenated on a single event. The client receives a final TCP RST from an upstream proxy, which in some cases appears to cause two last fragments to be merged and the expected end-marker ('data: [DONE]' or 'event: end') not delivered to the client.

Impact: User-facing partial outputs (last sentence/JSON object dropped or merged), downstream parsing failures in Acme Health's ingestion pipeline, several production jobs failing to mark documents complete. Affects ~3% of long-running streaming requests from the customer in us-east during high load windows.

Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated pool for Acme Health, using gpt-redwood-1-large, requests are SSE over HTTP/1.1 routed through our edge fleet behind a third-party transparent proxy (customer's infra fronting Redwood in their VPC).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided + internal repro):
1) Customer sends streaming SSE request with prompt that produces a long multi-paragraph response.
2) Reproduction easiest when the stream remains idle for >20s between tokens (simulating slow token emission).
3) If an upstream probe or NAT refresh causes abrupt TCP RST on the connection, the client sometimes receives the two trailing fragments concatenated into a single SSE 'data:' event and no explicit end event.
4) Local repro: curl --no-buffer to our SSE endpoint via an HAProxy instance configured with aggressive idle-timeout and probe.

Observed behavior: Partial/garbled JSON at stream end (two JSON fragments joined at boundary), parser errors in customer app, and no separate end-marker event. In some cases the client reconnects and requests resume but resume token cannot be applied correctly because the tail fragment lacks clear boundary markers.

Attachments: customer request IDs, sample SSE capture (redacted), edge access logs, haproxy config snippet provided by customer.
investigation_notes:
Timeline: Support triaged on 2026-03-10 after customer report. SRE collected edge and service logs for the window. Key findings:
- Edge TCP logs show the connection terminated with RST originating from the customer's upstream proxy within 50-200ms of last token emission in the failing sessions.
- Serving-runtime emitted two small chunks (chunk A and chunk B) within 30ms; the edge HTTP layer attempted to flush them as two SSE events.
- Packet capture at the edge shows the final two packets were delivered to the edge but the upstream RST caused the edge's downstream buffering layer to coalesce the two writes into a single downstream write that lacked an intermediate SSE delimiter (we observed missing additional '\n' between data frames).
- The SSE framing parser on the client side expects either a closing 'event: end'/'data: [DONE]' or a newline-separated set of 'data:' frames. When frames were concatenated without the separator, the client parsed as a single malformed JSON.

Hypothesis: Rapid upstream TCP resets combined with the edge's write-coalescing optimization and the edge-proxy's transparent TCP handling can drop delimiting newlines between buffered write segments, resulting in concatenated payloads and absent explicit end-marker delivery. The serving runtime itself completed generation and emitted the end marker; it did not see an error. The truncation/concatenation happens between the edge flush and network egress.

Tests performed:
- Reproduced locally using HAProxy idle-timeout 20s and curl; observed identical concatenation.
- Disabled write-coalescing on a staging edge node; concatenation rate dropped to 0/200 attempts.
- Instrumented edge to log write boundaries; logs correlate coalesced writes with upstream RST events and overloaded epoll wakeups.
comments: Support (Ana Martinez) - 2026-03-10: Opened after customer provided sample traces and example SSE fraction. Asked for exact request IDs and whether the customer saw any intermediary proxy or LB in their path.

Customer (Acme Health - DevOps) - 2026-03-10: Confirmed they run an HAProxy 2.4 instance with aggressive keepalive/health probe. Happy to reproduce with a test route. Reported failure rate ~3% for long streams during peak hours.

SRE (Marcus Lee) - 2026-03-11: Collected edge pcaps and confirmed RST timestamps. Added temporary log hooks to record write boundary metadata on edge nodes serving Acme. Hypothesis: edge coalescing + RST = lost delimiter.
Action: Disable Nagle/write-coalescing on selected edge nodes for Acme traffic as a mitigation; monitoring started.

Engineer (Priya Singh) - 2026-03-12: Verified serving-runtime always writes an end marker in the application layer. Created PR to ensure end marker is emitted as a separate flushable segment (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/6792). Also proposed an edge-layer sanitizer to insert a final '\n
' if missing on connection close.

Support (Ana Martinez) - 2026-03-12: Informed customer of temporary mitigation and asked them to relax HAProxy idle timeout to 90s as a quick fix. Customer agreed to test in their staging environment and will report results tomorrow.
resolution_notes:
Temporary mitigation: Disabled write-coalescing (SO_SNDBUF/Nagle adjustments) on three edge nodes routing Acme traffic and asked customer to increase HAProxy idle timeout to >=90s. After mitigation we observed reduction of incidents to 0.2% in the following 24h window.
Permanent fix plan:
- Short-term (next week): Merge PR that forces end-marker to be written and flushed as its own SSE event to reduce risk of coalescing-related loss (PR #6792).
- Mid-term: Add an edge-layer sanitizer that ensures delimiter sanity on connection close (insert missing '\n
' between write segments when RST/FIN observed) and instrument coalescing thresholds.
- Long-term: Update runbooks and add an internal test harness that simulates upstream RSTs to validate SSE behavior end-to-end.
Follow-ups: Create INT ticket for edge fleet config rollout (INT-20444) and add a Confluence runbook entry for customers with aggressive upstream proxies explaining recommended proxy settings for streaming workloads.
Status: mitigation applied and customer monitoring. Engineering change in progress.
